chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no Itikaf (seclusion) except with fasting in the general Masjid.

key_terms.اعْتِكَاف: Itikaf: Seclusion in a mosque for worship
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ الْجَامِعِ: Al-Masjid Al-Jami: The congregational or main mosque

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of Itikaf according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the legal validity of Itikaf by linking it inextricably to fasting, a condition emphasized in Shia jurisprudence to distinguish it from mere residence. By specifying the 'Masjid al-Jami' (congregational mosque), it underscores the communal aspect of this spiritual retreat, aligning with the scholarly view that Itikaf is an act of worship requiring both physical seclusion and devotional discipline.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no Itikaaf except with Fasting in the general Masjid’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Without fast and Jami‘ (central) Masjid Ttikaf is not valid.’”
